supersedes: locked_config_v5_ddr.json (renamed SUPERSEDED_; written 2026-09-23T14:03Z, before any DDR prediction existed, never used)
reason_for_revision: Framing clarified: the primary claim is intraset (within one deployment context, a second reader reduces missed PDR at a stated referral price, and site-measured complementarity and quality describe the benefit). DDR is analysed as a second site with operating points and measurements taken on DDR itself; applying EyePACS measurements to DDR (transport) becomes secondary. No DDR prediction existed when this revision was written.

depends_on.models: the 33 frozen v2 checkpoints (11 architectures x 3 seeds), trained on EyePACS only; no retraining, fine-tuning or recalibration on DDR
depends_on.preprocessing: recovered v1 pipeline used for every v2 set: RGB, resize 512x512 Lanczos, PNG; evaluation transform Resize 256, CenterCrop 224, ImageNet normalisation
depends_on.referral_probability: binary models: sigmoid of the single logit; 5-class models: softmax mass on grades 2 to 4

cohort.include: all DDR grading images with grade 0 to 4, DDR's own train, valid and test files pooled
cohort.byte_duplicates: within each group of byte-identical images keep one copy if labels agree, drop the group if labels disagree

grouping_and_split.purpose: DDR releases no patient identifier. Groups are defined from filenames only (label-free), coarse enough that both eyes of a patient fall in the same group under the assumptions stated, and are used as the unit for the intraset split and for cluster bootstrap intervals.
grouping_and_split.timestamp_named_images: 17-digit capture timestamp names: group = capture date (first 8 digits)
grouping_and_split.numbered_images: names of the form SSS-NNNN-XYZ: group = SSS plus floor(NNNN / 50), i.e. blocks of 50 consecutive image numbers
grouping_and_split.assumption_check_reported_not_decisive: grade agreement (quadratic-weighted kappa) for adjacent-number pairs and for timestamp pairs under 120 seconds apart, against random pairs. High agreement supports adjacency of fellow eyes; low agreement means the grouping may not hold fellow eyes together, and the intraset selection result is then flagged for possible optimistic leakage. Reported either way; does not change the analysis.
grouping_and_split.split: groups shuffled with seed 20260924 and assigned alternately to halves A and B, balancing image counts; file 01_splits/ddr_split_intraset_v2.csv written by the inference notebook before any prediction is made

operating_points.intraset_primary: each model refers its own top fraction f of images in the evaluated set, f = 1.31 x referable prevalence, prevalence measured on half A (the site's calibration data). 1.31 fixed from EyePACS (25% referral / 19.08% prevalence).
operating_points.fixed_25_percent_secondary: each model refers its own top 25%
operating_points.pre_registered_prediction: Fixed 25% sits below DDR referable prevalence (about 45%), the regime where APTOS showed most pairs losing at matched volume. Predicted: no benefit at fixed 25% matched volume; benefit at the prevalence-relative operating point.

primary_endpoints_intraset.P1_matched_volume_benefit: all included DDR images, operating point f: PDR eyes missed by the anchor minus PDR eyes missed by the max-percentile-rank ensemble referring the same fraction f, averaged over 110 ordered pairs and 9 seed combinations. Supported if the mean is positive and the group-cluster bootstrap 95% interval (2,000 resamples of groups) excludes zero.
primary_endpoints_intraset.P2_union_benefit_and_price: union rule at f: anchor-relative PDR rescued, incremental referrals and incremental false positives (grade 0 or 1) per pair, with cluster bootstrap intervals. Descriptive of the guaranteed benefit and its price; no hypothesis test on the rescued count, since it cannot be negative.

secondary_intraset_selection.predictors: C (ceiling-normalised severity-weighted complementarity), rho_cost and partner marginal cost, each measured on half A at operating point f, averaged over 9 seed combinations
secondary_intraset_selection.outcome: anchor-relative PDR rescued under the union rule at f, measured on half B
secondary_intraset_selection.statistics: within-anchor Spearman of C with the outcome, mean over 11 anchors, architecture bootstrap (1,000); partial on partner marginal; rule comparison (least overlap, least weighted dependence, best marginal, two-stage, random, oracle); paired differences against best marginal at matched volume and in incremental false positives
secondary_intraset_selection.two_stage_rule: restrict to partners whose half-A marginal cost is at most 1.10 x the lowest candidate marginal cost; choose the highest C among them; ties broken by lower marginal cost. Hypothesis generated from lock v4 confirmation (partial correlation 0.44); DDR is its first test.
secondary_intraset_selection.swap_sensitivity: repeat with halves exchanged (predictors on B, outcome on A); reported, not decisive

secondary_transport.T1: P1 and P2 at the fixed 25% operating point
secondary_transport.T2: partner ranking from EyePACS estimation-pool C (pair_quantities_estimation_v4.csv) against the DDR half-B outcome, same statistics as the intraset selection test

also_reported: grade 3 or worse in place of PDR
APTOS: exploratory only, not part of this lock
not_permitted: choosing any operating point, aggregation rule, grouping or subgroup after DDR predictions exist
recalibrating or thresholding models on DDR labels beyond the rank-based fractions defined here
printing or inspecting any DDR performance metric in the inference notebook
reporting the best DDR pair as a headline
confirmation_status: DDR predictions do not exist at the time of writing. The inference notebook asserts this file exists and predates every DDR prediction file; the analysis notebook is written only after inference completes and runs once.
